newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Audiolux says to cut Audiofina stake.
newsitem.headline: Audiolux says to cut Audiofina stake.

text.p: Luxembourg-based holding company Audiolux SA said in a statement on Friday it would reduce its stake in media holding Audiofina following a restructuring of its shareholder structure.
"The company has the intention to lighten its stake in Audiofina, which will allow it to invest in new projects," Audiolux said.
Audiofina owns 50 percent of Luxembourg media group CLT-UFA. The other 50 percent is held by Germany's Bertelsmann AG.

The statement was released ahead of an extraordinary general meeting of Audiolux shareholders, who were to vote on a reduction in the company's capital and an exchange of their holdings against Audiofina shares. Journalists were not admitted to the meeting.

Audiolux is offering its institutional shareholders Banque Generale du Luxembourg, Banque Paribas Luxembourg, BCEE and SNCI 19 Audiofina shares and around 5,600 Luxembourg francs in cash against their Audiolux shares, but has urged its private shareholders to remain with the company.

Following the transaction, Audiolux's biggest shareholder, holding company Luxempart together with insurance company La Foyer, will gain control of the company. Luxempart's chief executive officer was quoted last week as saying he wanted to make Audiolux a wider investment vehicle for the media sector.
In its statement on Friday, Audiolux's board said it would study "if interests held presently by Luxempart could be entirely or partially taken over by Audiolux."
Audiolux, which held around 5.2 percent of Audiofina at the end of 1996, will remain a listed company.
It was not immediately clear what stake Audiolux would have in Audiofina following the reduction in capital.
